inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL projection converts text to binary bytes, slices the converted value with LEFT, and converts the slice back to UTF-8.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent label-byte audit. Fixed multilingual labels undergo nested binary and utf8mb4 conversion with byte slices, while a short ASCII label verifies ordinary text behavior; hexadecimal projections make the byte-preserving result observable without copying source labels or schema.

fixture_notes: The multilingual label slices use byte lengths that end on complete UTF-8 characters: the first keeps two characters and the second keeps three. The ASCII label remains unchanged by the nested conversion.
determinism_notes: Labels, byte lengths, character sets, and ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE label_byte_samples (sample_id INT PRIMARY KEY, label_text VARCHAR(64) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO label_byte_samples (sample_id, label_text) VALUES (901, '霜時計'), (902, 'cabin')

steps.sql: SELECT sample_id, CONVERT(LEFT(CONVERT(label_text USING binary), CASE WHEN sample_id = 901 THEN 6 ELSE 3 END) USING utf8mb4) AS clipped_label, HEX(CONVERT(LEFT(CONVERT(label_text USING binary), CASE WHEN sample_id = 901 THEN 6 ELSE 3 END) USING utf8mb4)) AS clipped_hex FROM label_byte_samples ORDER BY sample_id
